summary:
June  


Thank you for your letter of June 14th regarding both my story collection for Ballantine and the over-due novel. 

I know you personally are aware of the basic reasons why the novel is over­ due: I was unable to write for two years after my previous wife and child left me, and have just resumed this year—doing first, of course, the completion on FLOW MY TEARS for Doubleday, which needed far less work to complete it than does the Ballantine one. And then I started SCANNER and got so hot on it that it wound up finished in the rough draft. Please tell Betty Ballantine that extreme personal miseries have been responsible for my long dry period—anyhow, to the point: I had not intended to do the final on SCANNER for some time (say possi­ bly a year from now) because Doubleday has no need for it until 1975; they will be publishing TEARS next year, so I would assume that would do it for that year re my novels. Therefore I will get back onto the Ballantine novel, which I had begun but then ceased working on when I flew to Canada—what I had written either got destroyed or stolen during my period up in Vancouver; anyhow none of it was in the stored boxes shipped down here last June, and now must be con­ sidered lost... like so much of my stuff in general.
